sourceAnchors.visualArbitrationNote: Printed page 474 opens the compact syndrome summary with the general statement that no or almost no reactions with `Triebüberdruck` occur in the source-defined Zwangsneurose pattern. The OCR derivative badly damages `Triebüberdruck`, so the admitted PDF governs the term.

Inside the worked Fall 40 analysis, Szondi states that the total absence of Quantumspannungsreaktionen is conditioned by increased ambivalence reactions and is also a `Kennzeichen der Zwangsvorgänge`. This is a stronger case-level formulation than the general p. 474 wording and must not replace it.

sourceExcerpt: Das totale Fehlen -von Quantumspannungsreaktionen wird durch die Erhöhung der Ambivalenzreaktionen bedingt
romanianRendering: La p. 474, regula generală pentru configurația Zwangsneurose este absența sau aproape absența reacțiilor cu Triebüberdruck. În Fall 40, Szondi descrie forma mai puternică: absența totală a Quantumspannungsreaktionen, pe care o leagă de creșterea Ambivalenzreaktionen și o numește de asemenea Kennzeichen der Zwangsvorgänge. Exemplul nu suprascrie formularea generală.
doctrinalStatement: În syndromatica source-defined a Zwangsneurose, afirmația generală este `keine oder fast keine Reaktionen mit Triebüberdruck`. Separat, în analiza Fall 40, Szondi afirmă `totales Fehlen von Quantumspannungsreaktionen`, îl leagă de creșterea Ambivalenzreaktionen și îl numește `Kennzeichen der Zwangsvorgänge`. Relația din Fall 40 rămâne o calificare/exemplificare mai puternică în interiorul modelului Szondi; nu transformă absența totală într-o condiție necesară și nu transformă explicația prin ambivalență într-o lege cauzală generală modernă.
conditions: For the general syndrome statement, inspect Quantumspannungsreaktionen/Triebüberdruck at series level rather than a single isolated reaction.
Keep the general p. 474 wording (`keine oder fast keine`) distinct from the stronger total-absence statement made in Fall 40.
Read the Fall 40 ambivalence relation together with the worked case and the other Zwang syndrome components.
exceptions: Do not require total absence of Quantumspannungsreaktionen as a necessary condition for the general source-defined Zwangsneurose pattern.
Do not infer Zwangsneurose solely from absent or sparse Quantumspannungsreaktionen.
Do not treat the Fall 40 statement that increased ambivalence conditions total absence of Quantumspannung as a contemporary universal causal mechanism.
Do not equate all low-quantum series with the historical Zwangsneurose pattern.
scopeNotes: The general p. 474 statement and the stronger Fall 40 formulation are deliberately retained at different levels of generality.
Fall 40 remains a worked source example; its total-absence configuration is not promoted into an obligatory syndrome threshold.
This record may later be reviewed against existing P1 quantum-tension calculations, but remains non-executable.
